title: Level design
description: When things happen in a level. The level SVG's layer names say where and what; this file says when. It is a small state machine: each state lists what happens on entering it, and `next` lists the events that move it on. Nothing here is a coordinate: places are named by layer path, such as "RESTRICTED-import-export-warehouse/ENTER-building".

$schema.description: Path to this schema, for editor autocomplete and hover help.

version.description: Format version. A file without it is read as a draft and migrated in memory, with warnings.

start.description: The state the level begins in. Must be a key of `states`.

groups.description: Spawn groups defined once, for any state to spawn by name: spawn type, then group name, then the group's keys. A state's spawn names the group in `group` and its own keys win, key by key; a list (`pool`, `order`) is replaced whole.

cases.description: Named flags for the level. Each is a starting true or false that states change with `set`, or { "condition": ... } to follow from the start, such as "has-key": { "condition": "inventory:key" }. Triggers, `when` and locks read them as "case:<name>"; turning true reports "case:<name>".

restricted.description: Unlock conditions for RESTRICTED-<name> layers, keyed by <name>. Overrides a REQUIRE- layer inside it. A RESTRICTED layer with no condition here or in the SVG stays locked.

until.description: Locked until this is true, for example "case:enemies-defeated" or "state:boss-down". Reports "unlock:<name>" when it opens.

type.description: "once" (default): opens the first time `until` holds and stays open for the run. "condition": open while `until` holds, locked again (reporting "lock:<name>") when it stops.

look.description: What LOOK on the command line says about things, by layer name: an OBJECT-, BREAKABLE-, ENTERABLE- or RESTRICTED- (for its door) or INVENTORY- layer. Without one, a thing is named by its layer name in words ("parking gate box").

states.description: The level's states, keyed by name. Entering one reports "state:<name>".

name.description: A state, case, group or layer name: letters, digits, - and _.

trigger.description: "<kind>:<key>" for any level event (break:, enter:, exit:, interact:, animate:, event:, locked:, unlock:, lock:, spawn:<group>, defeated:<group>, fled:<group> when any of a group ran off, arrive:<state> once the player has come on for that state, take:<item>, use:<item>, drop:<item>, combine:<item> each time the player does it with an item, look:<name> and talk:<name> from the command line), or "case:<name>" (that case is true) or "state:<name>" (that state was entered).

layerPath.description: A layer named by its map id, optionally under its nearest mapped parent: "ENTER-building" or "RESTRICTED-import-export-warehouse/ENTER-building". Illustrator's numbered copies ("ENTER-building-2") match their base name.

svg.description: What the level art does on entering the state. "loads" and "none": nothing, the scene as it is. "layer-state-change": a marker that the art changes through the layers themselves, such as a breakable's _broken art. "fade-out": fade to black and back, then place the player.

set.description: Cases to change on entering the state. Cases not listed keep their value. Each change reports "case:<name>" when the case becomes true.

cases.description: From entering this state on, these cases follow a condition (until a later state gives another, or `set`s them). Each must be in the top `cases`, which gives its value until then.

spawn.description: Groups of characters to bring in on entering the state.

animate-layers.description: Layers of the level art to slide on entering the state, such as a door's glass. Each is cut out of the background and keeps its place in the stacking order, so art drawn over it in Illustrator stays over it. Reports "animate:<layer>" when it gets where it was sent.

characters.description: Planned. Friendly and neutral characters are not built yet; a value other than false warns.

next.description: What moves the level on from this state. Only the current state's steps are live, and the first to fire wins.

when.description: Cases that must have these values for the step to fire, such as { "has-key": true }. With no `on`, the step fires as soon as they do.

to.description: The state to move to. Must be a key of `states`.

player.description: What happens to the player on entering the state.

spawn.description: Where the player is placed: "left" or "right" edge of the walkable area, or a layer path. Leave out to keep the player where they are.

animation.description: How the player arrives. "walk" walks in from the spawn side; "idle" appears standing.

inventory.description: What the player carries: "empty" empties it, "inherit" keeps it, "store" keeps it and saves it for the next level.

health.description: "full" refills it, "inherit" keeps it, "store" saves it for the next level.

spawnGroup.description: A group to bring in. Its keys may come from a group of the same name under `groups`; the ones written here win. `type` and `from` are needed here or there.

group.description: The group's name, and the group under `groups` it spawns, if there is one. Reports "spawn:<group>" when the first one appears and "defeated:<group>" when all of them are done.

type.description: What to spawn. Only "enemy" is built. May be left out when the group is defined under `groups`.

count.description: How many to spawn. Left out: every enemy the pool brings (each entry its own `count`), or 1 with no pool.

pick.description: "random": each one is drawn from the pool, without repeats while the pool lasts. "in-order": the pool's ids in turn.

pool.description: The enemies to choose from: an enemy's id or art name ("jumpingjunkie" or "JumpingJunkie"), or { "enemy", "render" } for one drawn with some parts recolored. Leave out for every enemy that is not a sub-boss or boss in any stage.

anyOf.description: An enemy's id or art name, in any case.

from.description: Where they come in: a layer they come out of, such as a door (they appear at its foot and walk down into the walkable area), or "edges": from just off the view's left and right edges, taking turns.

animation.description: How they arrive. "walk" walks them out of the layer before their AI starts; "idle" starts the AI at once.

after.description: Seconds after entering the state before the first one appears.

every.description: Seconds between each one after the first. Not used when they come out all at once (`order` "same"). Also read when written "timeout", with a note.

then.description: What they do once out. "fight" (default), or "flee": stand a moment, run off the nearer edge of the view and are gone; the group then reports "fled:<group>" instead of "defeated:<group>".

inherit.description: true: bring back the members of this group's last spawn still standing, wherever they are, with the health they had, instead of new ones. `count`, `pick`, `pool` and `order` are not used.

groupDef.description: A spawn group defined once. Any spawn key but `group` and `type`, which are where it is filed. A state's spawn of this group lays its own keys over these.

order.description: The order the members `pick` chose come out in. "random": shuffled. "sequence": pool order. "reverse": the other way. "same" (or "load"): all at once. A list: those names first (a pool entry's `name`, an enemy's id or art name, or a pool position from 1), then the rest in pool order. Left out: all at once when the state was entered through a door, otherwise the order `pick` drew them in.

poolEnemy.description: An enemy in a pool written as an object: how many of it, how many of those drawn with some of their parts recolored, and a name for `order` lists. Each has the enemy's own stats.

enemy.description: The enemy: its id or art name, in any case.

count.description: How many of this enemy the entry brings.

re-render.description: How many of `count` are drawn with `render`; the rest are drawn as the enemy is. Left out: all of them.

name.description: A name for this entry, for `order` lists and the debug box, such as "gray-crimeguy".

render.description: Part name (a layer name in the enemy's art, such as "left-vest") to palette name (in config/palettes.json, such as "gray"). Every shape in the part takes the palette's color for its tone, read from its layer name ("vest-mid" is mid). A frame without a sided part ("left-vest") uses the bare one ("vest").

layer.description: The layer to move, by its name in the art (any layer, not only a map id), optionally under layers it sits in: "door-glass-left" or "ENTER-building/door-glass-left". Illustrator's numbered copies ("door-glass-left-2") match their base name.

position-x.description: Where it goes across, measured from where the art draws it, in the level SVG's units (Illustrator's). Negative is left. Leave out to keep it where it is across; 0 puts it back.

position-y.description: Where it goes up or down, measured from where the art draws it, in the level SVG's units. Negative is up. Leave out to keep it where it is; 0 puts it back.

type.description: How it travels: "linear" at one speed, "ease-in" starting slow, "ease-out" ending slow, "ease-in-out" both.

duration.description: Seconds it takes to get there. 0 or left out: at once.

after.description: Seconds after entering the state before it starts.

condition.description: <source>[:<name>] [<op> <whole number>], read every frame. Counts: "alive" (enemies in play, standing or still to come, in every scene), "alive:<group>" (that group still to beat; before it starts, all it will bring), "fled:<group>", "inventory:<item>", "inventory". With no op, a count means at least 1. Flags, true or false with no op: "case:<name>", "state:<name>" (entered). Ops: = != < <= > >=.

caseCondition.description: A case that follows a condition instead of holding a value.

reset.description: What entering the state puts back as it was at the start of the run, each able to report again: "break:<name>" (whole again), "animate:<layer>" (back where the art draws it), "unlock:<name>" (locked again), "case:<name>" (its starting value). Or "level": the whole run, then the start state.
